findings.title: Integration test queries denormalized table that may not contain created records
findings.body: The test creates a booking via `prisma.booking.create({...})` (lines 456-466) but the final query targets `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` (line 482). `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` is a separate denormalized table/view typically populated via triggers, materialized view refresh, or background jobs - it is not automatically populated by inserting a `Booking` row. If the sync is not configured or has not run in the test environment, the query will return `[]` and `expect(results).toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])` will fail for reasons unrelated to the SQL conditions under test. This makes the test unreliable as a real validation of the constructed SQL. Either insert directly into `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized`, trigger whatever sync the production code relies on, or assert against a table that reflects the data immediately. The previous `findMany`-based test had the same dependency, but converting it to `$queryRaw` made the dependency more explicit and did nothing to address it.

findings.title: Public `findMany` method removed without updating callers in this PR
findings.body: The service previously exposed `async findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` and is now replaced with `getBaseConditions()` returning `Prisma.Sql`. This is a breaking change to the class's public surface. The diff does not show updates to other callers in the repo (e.g. any API route, tRPC procedure, or service consumer that imported `InsightsBookingService` and called `.findMany(...)`); those imports will fail to compile after this lands. A maintainer should grep the codebase for `InsightsBookingService` consumers and migrate them, or keep a delegating `findMany` wrapper to preserve backward compatibility.

findings.title: Caching behavior is now untested
findings.body: The class still caches `cachedAuthConditions` (line 49) and `cachedFilterConditions` (line 50), and the getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions methods still gate their build behind `=== undefined` (lines 84-87 and 91-94). However, the entire `describe("Caching", ...)` block that previously verified (a) the first call builds conditions and (b) the second call returns the cached value with reference equality was removed by this PR. There is no remaining coverage proving the cache works, that two concurrent calls don't both populate it (a small race exists because the read-then-await-then-assign sequence is not atomic), or that the cached Prisma.Sql values are still usable as raw query fragments after the assignment. At minimum the deleted cache tests should be ported to the new `Prisma.sql` comparison style.

findings.title: Dead branch in getBaseConditions: authConditions is always truthy
findings.body: `buildAuthorizationConditions` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` value (either a real condition or `NOTHING_CONDITION`), never null/undefined. Therefore `authConditions` in `getBaseConditions` is always truthy, and the `else if (filterConditions)` branch on line 76 is unreachable - it can only execute if `authConditions` is falsy, which never happens. This is not a functional bug (the conditions still resolve correctly) but it indicates a misread of the type contract and leaves misleading code. Either remove the dead branch and the unreachable `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION; }`, or change `getAuthorizationConditions` to return `Prisma.Sql | null` and return `NOTHING_CONDITION` explicitly only at call sites, so the truthiness checks become meaningful.
